findings.title: f64-download claim is false against existing code; wire serialization silently depends on it
findings.description: The design states "`export_positions()` and `export_velocities()` return f64 arrays (Quadrants upcasts on download). The `TickResult` therefore carries f64, preserving the downstream contract," and success criterion A3 rests on this ("Downstream code (`client_manager.broadcast`, sim logger) requires zero changes"). The substrate code contradicts this: `src/migratory/bench/backends/quadrants_fused_state.py:228` declares `export_positions() -> NDArray[np.float32]` and ends with `np.column_stack([x, y]).astype(np.float32, copy=False)` — the field is `qd.f32` and there is no upcast anywhere in the download path (`export_velocities` and `export_profile_indices` likewise). `TickResult.from_quadrants_fields` (`src/migratory/engine/tick_result.py:124`) explicitly documents that slice-145 backends pass f32 arrays through with only a `type: ignore`. If an f32 array reaches `protocol.serialize_state_update` (`src/migratory_server/protocol.py:185-186`), `np.ascontiguousarray` preserves dtype and `.tobytes()` emits 4-byte floats under a header whose format is documented as `positions_f64`; `deserialize_message` reads `<f8`, producing truncated/garbage wire frames. The design as written would implement no conversion, unit test 5 asserts only `count` and finiteness (no dtype), so A3 would ship unverified and the wire would be corrupted. The design must specify an explicit `astype(np.float64)` (or an equivalent cast at the `TickResult` construction boundary) and assert dtype in the A3 test.

findings.title: REFLECT velocity flip is never synced back to the GPU
findings.description: The sync-back mechanism (`notify_positions_modified(positions)` → `upload_positions`) transfers positions only. `_apply_reflect` (`src/migratory_server/bounds_enforcement.py`) mutates *velocities* in place as well (outward velocity sign-flip at the boundary). On the GPU path that flip stays on the host; the GPU-resident velocities keep pointing outward forever, so each tick integrates agents into the wall and the host clamps them back — agents pin at the boundary with a persistently outward velocity, diverging from the NumPy reference behavior. This violates the architecture's first design goal ("Preserve behavioral fidelity across scaling tiers … verifiable against the current NumPy implementation"), and A4 only asserts positions are finite/in-bounds, so the test suite would not catch it. Either extend the sync-back to velocities for REFLECT, or state explicitly why velocity divergence is acceptable. Related: the stated rule "call `notify_positions_modified` on any non-OPEN policy" fires for SOFT as well, but `apply_bounds_policy` is a no-op for SOFT (`bounds_enforcement.py` case `BoundsPolicy.SOFT: return`) — that would add a pointless per-tick upload and contradicts the Open Notes claim that the extra transfer occurs only "when bounds enforcement modifies positions."

findings.title: Spawn/despawn sync is under-specified and as described would revert GPU-advanced state
findings.description: The slice plan entry assigns this slice "spawn/despawn (re-upload changed agent state)," and the design's mechanism is `count_changed_since_last_tick()` → `sync_from_entity_manager()` described as "Re-upload CPU state after spawn/despawn." Three gaps: (1) a full CPU→GPU re-upload on any count change overwrites every agent's positions/velocities with the *stale* CPU mirror (which the GPU path never updates after setup), reverting the whole flock to its initial state on the first spawn/despawn; only the new/shifted agents need uploading, but the design does not specify a partial upload. (2) `setup_from_server()` sizes fields with `n = entity_manager.count`, while the server's real bound is `entity_capacity` (`config.py:1207`, enforced in `entities.py:79`) — a post-startup spawn past `n` has nowhere to land in the fixed `qd.root.dense(qd.i, n)` allocation. (3) `remove_entity` (`entities.py:175`) compacts arrays and shifts indices; the GPU state ordering is never remapped, so profile indices and `leadership_per_agent` would misalign after a removal. The unit test only asserts the subsequent tick "does not raise," which none of these failure modes would trigger. Specify the partial-upload semantics, the field-capacity policy (size to `entity_capacity`, or realloc), and index remapping — or explicitly scope runtime spawn/despawn out and say how the startup-only `spawn_population` path is covered.

findings.title: Snapshot path reads the stale CPU mirror on the GPU path
findings.description: `make_snapshot_builder` (`src/migratory_server/clients.py:361`) builds its `TickResult` from `TickResult.from_numpy_state(em.state, em.count)` — the CPU `AgentState`. On the GPU path the CPU arrays are never written after `setup_from_server()`, so any client connecting mid-run receives a SNAPSHOT of tick-0 positions followed by STATE_UPDATEs from the live GPU tick (absolute-vs-incremental desync). A3 claims `client_manager.broadcast` needs zero changes, but does not mention this second consumer of `em.state`; the design asserts "the world server call site (`server.py`) is unchanged" without addressing which structure is the source of truth once the GPU owns state. Either download GPU state for snapshots, mirror positions back to `entity_manager.state` each tick (cost on the hot path — must be justified), or explicitly document the staleness bound.

findings.title: `_select_arch()` selects by platform, contradicting A7's "no GPU" fallback requirement
findings.description: A7 requires: "A host with no Metal and no CUDA starts successfully … `_select_arch()` falls back to `qd.cpu` and logs a WARNING." The given `_select_arch()` only inspects `platform.system()` — any Linux host returns `qd.cuda` without checking that a CUDA device or driver exists. On a GPU-less Linux box, `qd.init(arch=qd.cuda)` raises, and the Open Notes explicitly embrace that ("the server exits at startup with a clear error. There is no mid-session recovery path — a GPU failure after startup is fatal"). The two statements are irreconcilable: as designed, the exact host A7 targets (no Metal, no CUDA) crashes instead of falling back. The slice plan entry also says "if neither is *detected*" — detection, not platform assumption. Either probe for device availability before selecting (and fall back to `qd.cpu` on failure of `qd.init`), or narrow A7 to the platform cases the code actually detects.

findings.title: Verification walkthrough "CPU default (no GPU)" contradicts the default-is-quadrants rule
findings.description: Step 1 says "Remove the `compute:` block entirely (or set `backend: cpu`). … No GPU initialization should appear in logs." With `ComputeConfig.backend` defaulting to `"quadrants"` (and `default.yaml`'s block only commented out), removing the block yields the *quadrants* path and the `GPU compute backend: quadrants (arch=…)` log line **will** appear — the walkthrough's expected outcome is wrong for the first half of its own disjunction. Only `backend: cpu` produces the stated result.

findings.title: Files Changed lists a non-existent file path
findings.description: `src/migratory_server/entity_manager.py` does not exist; `EntityManager` lives in `src/migratory_server/entities.py`. The `count_changed_since_last_tick()` row should name the real file (the same row's class name is correct).
